text: Toehold switches function by having the trigger RNA sequester the ribosome binding site in a hairpin, which is then released only when the target mRNA is degraded by RNase E.
explanation: This is false on two counts: it is the toehold switch RNA itself (not the trigger RNA) that forms the hairpin sequestering the RBS and start codon, and release occurs when the trigger RNA base-pairs with an exposed linear toehold region and unfolds the hairpin -- not through RNase E-mediated degradation. This trigger-induced conformational unfolding is what exposes the RBS and allows translation to begin, making toehold switches programmable, cell-free-compatible biosensors.
